title: Replay Failures as Successes: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Instruction Following
claim: Binary and aggregated rewards give sparse or indistinguishable signals on hard tasks; our method trains small models to rival frontier ones.
layout: 3 panels: two left illustrated cartoons, two right bar charts; dashed divider
description: The left half has two cartoon panels separated by a dashed red line. Each has a pink banner and an emoji face. The first reads 'Train with binary rewards: Unable to solve difficult tasks.' It shows a broken robot surrounded by labels for insufficient successful samples, sparse rewards and weak capacity. Beside the robot are two instruction checklists scored 1.0 with a green check and 0.0 with a red cross. The second panel reads 'Train with aggregated rewards: Distinct criteria, identical rewards.' A confused robot with '??' is labeled with neglected criteria, ambiguous rewards and a distorted learning target. Two partly checked checklists both score 0.5 with orange badges. The right half has two bar charts, IFBench and MuLDimIF. In each, the blue 'Ours' bar is highlighted and sits first, with the highest value labeled in blue, next to grey bars for frontier LLMs with logos.
caption: (Left) A conceptual illustration of the sparse and indistinguishable reward problem in current RLVR methods for instruction following tasks. (Right) Performance comparison between small LLMs trained by HiR and frontier LLMs on different benchmarks.
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has shown promise for aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) to follow instructions with various constraints. Despite the encouraging results, RL improvement inevitably relies on sampling successful, high-quality responses; however, the initial model often struggles to generate responses that satisfy all constraints due to its limited capabilities, yielding sparse or indistinguishable rewards that impede learning. In this work, we propose Hindsight instruction Replay (HiR), a novel sample-efficient RL framework for complex instruction following tasks, which employs a select-then-rewrite strategy to replay failed attempts as successes based on the constraints that have been satisfied in hindsight. We perform RL on these replayed samples as well as the original ones, theoretically framing the objective as dual-preference learning at both the instruction- and response-level to enable efficient optimization using only a binary reward signal. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed HiR yields promising results across different instruction following tasks, while requiring less computational budget. Our code and dataset is available at https://github.com/sastpg/HIR.
